versions.changelog: Fix exit trigger keywords, add phrase overrides (开始/学习/认识), add validate_format.js, document 了 verb limitation, verify pinyin-pro is MIT licensed

- Updated documentation to clarify that the pinyin-pro dependency is now MIT-licensed and free to use, instead of requiring a commercial license.
- Other instructions and usage notes were adjusted to reflect the new open source licensing status.
- No changes to functionality; documentation only.

Version 1.2.0

- Manual trigger clarified: Pinyin mode now starts and stops only via explicit user keywords (e.g., "进入儿童模式"/"退出儿童模式"), not automatic detection.
- Added instructions and an explicit example for reverting to single-line, plain Chinese after exiting pinyin mode.
- Updated installation instructions: now documents the npm install step and clarifies that "pinyin-pro" requires a commercial license.
- Noted limitations with emoji alignment, especially for multi-codepoint/flag/skin-tone emojis.
- Documentation reorganized and expanded for clarity, including script paths and commercial dependencies.

- Added explicit "exit triggers" for leaving child/pinyin mode, including instructions to resume normal (non-pinyin) format when requested.
- Clarified that emoji and symbols are displayed identically on both pinyin and Chinese lines for format consistency.
- Added fallback handling guidance for rare or unsupported characters in the output.
- Improved documentation for when and how to consistently use (or stop using) the two-line pinyin format.

Version 1.1.0 – Improved polyphonic word handling and script packaging

- Enhanced to use phrase-level (up to 4 characters) pinyin matching, reducing common polyphonic errors.
- Added a built-in override dictionary covering frequent word and character pronunciation pitfalls.
- Introduced npm packaging for the script for easier installation and dependency management.
- Updated documentation to reflect improved matching logic and override examples.

No user-facing changes.

- Internal update to scripts/to_pinyin.js; no changes to user documentation or skill behavior.
- Version bump to 1.0.9.

- Internal code changes in scripts/to_pinyin.js; no user-facing documentation updates.
- Maintains all existing functionality and usage patterns described in SKILL.md.

chinese-pinyin-display v1.0.7

- Added explicit dependency note for pinyin-pro in the documentation.
- No changes to core logic; clarifies which npm package to use for accurate polyphonic word handling.

- Added English translations/explanations alongside all key Chinese instructions and error cases.
- Clarified format consistency requirements and validation rules in both Chinese and English.
- Improved descriptions of common mistakes and critical scenarios where format consistency is at risk.
- No changes to code or functionality; documentation update only.

- Documentation updated: Added clarification on format recovery and requirements for handling formatting mistakes.
- Now explicitly instructs users to immediately resend any message with correct two-line pinyin/character format if a formatting error occurs.
- No changes to core functionality or code; SKILL.md only.

- Added a new detailed section on format consistency requirements and common mistakes, including real-world error examples.
- Emphasized the importance of maintaining strict two-line (pinyin + characters) output for all replies in children's mode.
- Clarified rules for when and how to use the skill, and provided guidance on handling exceptional cases.
- No changes to code or functionality; documentation update only.

- Added a new section describing automatic triggers for pinyin display (e.g., entering children's mode, requests for pinyin).
- Clarified when and how the skill is activated for different learning scenarios. 
- No changes to code or output—documentation improvement only.

- Updated the description to be more concise and bilingual for improved clarity.
- No logic or code changes; documentation only.

- Added full Chinese translation alongside English for all documentation sections.
- Expanded description and trigger phrases to include Chinese terms (e.g., “汉语拼音”).
- Provided bilingual examples, rules, usage instructions, and context information.
- Clarified key concepts and format requirements in both languages.

- Initial release of chinese-pinyin-display skill.
- Displays Chinese text with pinyin pronunciation in a structured two-line format: top line pinyin (syllable-spaced), bottom line Chinese characters.
- Ensures matching structure and spacing between pinyin and character lines, including punctuation.
- Includes phrase overrides for correct polyphonic pronunciations (e.g., 小龙虾 as xiǎo lóng xiā).
- Meant for children's literacy and pinyin learning; triggers on keywords like “儿童模式”, “拼音模式”, “display with pinyin”.
